site.description: Louis-Simon Guité is a PhD researcher in astrophysics at CEA Paris-Saclay. Publications, posters and CV.
site.intro: I am an astrophysics PhD researcher studying solar and stellar magnetic activity, star-planet magnetic interactions, and sympathetic flares. Combining magnetohydrodynamic and radiative transfer modeling with space-based observations and statistical analysis, my work explores how planets or sungrazer comets interact with magnetized stellar winds, how can these magnetic interactions deposit energy in stellar atmospheres, and how solar active regions interact with each other to trigger flares.

publications.title: Sungrazing comets as analogs of star-planet magnetic interactions
publications.authors: L-S. Guité, A. Strugarek, A.J. Finley, S. Parenti, V. Réville, A. Paul, A.S. Brun, J. de Carpentier
publications.summary: In this paper, we investigated wether a sungrazer comet passing through the Sun's corona, in this case comet Lovejoy in December 2011, could spark solar activity through magnetic interactions similar to those studied in star–exoplanet systems (SPMI; star-planet magnetic interactions). By combining coronal wind MHD simulations with solar EUV observations and magnetic interaction scaling laws, we found that the comet's direct magnetic power is too weak to drive a brightening on its own, though it may still perturb coronal magnetic fields and help trigger flares. Future sungrazing comets offer a promising natural laboratory to test these star–planet-like interactions up close.

publications.title: Avalanching Together: A Model for Sympathetic Flaring
publications.authors: L-S. Guité, P. Charbonneau, A. Strugarek
publications.summary: We modeled sympathetic solar flares using a coupled two-lattice self-organized critical avalanche framework to represent interacting active regions, finding that stronger coupling increases short waiting times and energy synchronization. Comparing the model's waiting-time statistics with solar observations indicates that any magnetic coupling driving sympathetic flares between active regions is likely relatively weak.

figure.caption: Connectivity and transfer between two avalanche model lattices

publications.title: Flaring together: A preferred angular separation between sympathetic flares on the Sun
publications.authors: L-S. Guité, A. Strugarek, P. Charbonneau
publications.summary: Analyzing large flare catalogs from SDO/AIA, RHESSI, and Solar Orbiter/STIX across solar cycles 24 and 25, we found strong statistical evidence for sympathetic solar flares, occurring at roughly a 5% rate, with an excess of same-hemisphere pairs separated by ~30° in longitude within 1.5 hours, alongside a deficit of certain transequatorial pairs (unsympathetic flares?). Magnetic extrapolations of field-line footpoint separations help explain this characteristic angular scale.

figure.caption: Sympathetic flares and magnetic connectivity between two solar active regions
